skill.name: kvkk-denetim
skill.description: Reviews Turkish KVKK privacy notices, consent text, and data practices for common compliance gaps. Includes templates, checklist guidance, and a local Python quick-check script.
skill.summary: Audit Turkish KVKK privacy notices, consent forms, and data practices.
skill.author: cesareth

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fenced examples in SKILL.md. I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or business-logic abuse. The bundled Python script performs local text and file analysis only.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md lines 75-102 are a Markdown fenced privacy notice template. The backticks delimit sample legal text and are not executable Ruby or shell code.
SKILL.md lines 102-106 only close one Markdown template and open another. There is no command interpreter, shell invocation, or user-controlled execution path.
SKILL.md lines 106-117 are a Markdown fenced explicit consent template. The fenced content contains legal prose placeholders, not shell commands.
SKILL.md lines 117-143 contain a closing Markdown fence and explanatory compliance text. No executable command or Ruby backtick expression is present.
SKILL.md lines 143-161 are a fenced report output example. It is a documentation template, not shell or Ruby execution.

content.value_statement: Turkish teams need fast checks for KVKK notices, consent forms, and privacy policies. This skill reviews required elements, flags gaps, and drafts practical compliance text.
actual_capabilities: Guides KVKK audits with checklists for data inventory, legal basis, notices, rights, and security.
Drafts Turkish aydınlatma metni and explicit consent templates using provided placeholders.
Reviews privacy text for missing controller, purpose, transfer, retention, contact, and Article 11 rights.
Uses the included Python script to score text or file inputs against keyword-based KVKK checks.
References core KVKK articles and common violations from bundled reference material.
limitations: It is informational and does not replace licensed legal advice.
Penalty amounts and legal thresholds may become outdated without manual updates.
The quick-check script is keyword-based and can miss nuanced legal issues.
It focuses on Turkish KVKK requirements, not full GDPR compliance.

use_cases.title: Review Product Data Flows
use_cases.description: Check app signup, support, and analytics data flows before publishing a privacy notice.

use_cases.title: Find Notice Gaps
use_cases.description: Identify missing KVKK Article 10 and Article 11 elements in existing customer notices.

use_cases.title: Draft First Policies
use_cases.description: Create a first draft of an aydınlatma metni and explicit consent statement.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Privacy Notice
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Turkish privacy notice for KVKK Article 10 completeness. List missing elements, risk level, and plain-language fixes: [paste text]

prompt_templates.title: Draft Consent Text
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate drafting for a clear purpose
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Turkish explicit consent statement for this processing activity. Include data type, purpose, withdrawal right, date, name, and signature fields: [describe activity]

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Service Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this service workflow for KVKK compliance. Check data inventory, legal basis, transfers, retention, Article 11 rights, and security controls: [describe workflow]

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Remediation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the KVKK checklist and reference articles to produce a prioritized remediation plan. Group findings by critical, important, and recommended actions: [paste audit notes]

output_examples.input: A privacy notice has no retention period and does not mention Article 11 rights.
output_examples.output: Critical gaps: Article 11 rights are missing. Important gaps: retention details are missing. Suggested fix: add rights, contact method, and retention schedule.

output_examples.input: A consent form says users accept data processing by using the service.
output_examples.output: Finding: consent is likely invalid because passive use is not explicit consent. Suggested fix: request separate, informed, and withdrawable consent.

output_examples.input: A service uses Stripe and Google Cloud for Turkish customer data.
output_examples.output: Important issue: possible international transfer. Review KVKK Article 9 requirements, transfer notices, legal basis, and provider safeguards.

best_practices: Provide the full Turkish text and describe the real data flow before asking for review.
Validate generated legal text with a qualified Turkish privacy lawyer before publication.
Keep KVKK penalty amounts, VERBİS thresholds, and regulatory guidance current.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the generated report as binding legal advice.
Do not use generic GDPR wording without adapting it to KVKK requirements.
Do not rely only on keyword checks for high-risk or special-category data processing.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides informational review and drafting support. A qualified lawyer should approve final compliance decisions.

faq.question: Can it create a KVKK aydınlatma metni?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a template and can draft text from your company, purpose, data, transfer, and contact details.

faq.question: Can it review existing privacy policies?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks for common KVKK elements, missing rights, unclear transfers, retention gaps, and risky consent language.

faq.question: Does it work for GDPR compliance?
faq.answer: No. It may compare KVKK and GDPR at a high level, but it focuses on Turkish KVKK requirements.

faq.question: Does the script send data to external services?
faq.answer: No evidence found. The included Python script reads local text or file input and prints a local report.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the notice text, processed data types, processing purposes, recipients, retention period, transfer details, and contact method.
